scope: Proposition 2.4 (Marked cascade recursion) of the manuscript “All-temperature pressure for orthogonally invariant Ising spin glasses” (preprints/All-temperature-pressure-for-orthogonally-invariant-Ising-spin-glasses-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 234 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ecaeb31108feca6f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Give the root a random mark η0. Conditional on ancestor marks, give each child at level i a mark with probability kernel Ki(dηi | η0, . . . , ηi−1), independently for distinct children, for 1 ≤ i ≤ k − 1. All marks are independent of the Poisson processes conditional on their ancestors. One may also integrate a residual mark ηk at each leaf, with kernel Kk, afresh on every visit to that leaf. For a measurable payoff X(η0, . . . , ηk) define Xk−1 = log ∫︂ eX dKk, Xi−1 = 1 ζi log ∫︂ eζiXi dKi (i = k − 1, . . . , 1). Here X = −∞ is allowed on excluded residual states, so the leaf integral can impose a hard constraint without renormalizing its prior; the integral itself must be strictly positive and finite. If there is no residual mark, set Xk−1 = X instead. Assume that all these quantities are finite real numbers almost surely under the original path law, and that E|X0| < ∞. Then E log ∑︂ α ναeXk−1(α) = EX0. (2.3) After tilting the leaf masses by eXk−1 , the unmarked cascade has its original law up to tree relabeling. Conditional on the branching of sampled leaves, their marks use the kernels d˜︂ Ki = eζi(Xi−Xi−1) dKi (1 ≤ i ≤ k − 1), d˜︂ Kk = eX−Xk−1 dKk. (2.4) The root mark keeps its original law: the Gibbs probability is normalized for each fixed root mark, and the outer expectation still averages that mark under its original distribution. Different branches use conditionally independent marks, and separate visits use independent residual marks even when their leaf labels coincide. These assertions hold for every bounded measurable test of the sampled branching and marks.
